problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w={x}^{2}yz+x{y}^{2}z+xy{z}^{2}$ at the point $(1,-1,1,-1).$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz+x{y}^{2}z+xy{z}^{2})=2xyz+{y}^{2}z+y{z}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}yz+x{y}^{2}z+xy{z}^{2})={x}^{2}z+2xyz+x{z}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}yz+x{y}^{2}z+xy{z}^{2})={x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2}+2xyz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1) & =2(1)(-1)(1)+(-1)^{2}(1)+(-1)(1)^{2}=-2 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1) & =(1)^{2}(1)+2(1)(-1)(1)+(1)(1)^{2}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1) & =(1)^{2}(-1)+(1)(-1)^{2}+2(1)(-1)(1)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-(-1) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1)+(y-(-1))\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1) \\ w+1 & =-2(x-1)+0\cdot (y+1)-2(z-1) \\ w+1 & =-2x-2z+4 \\ 2x+2z+w-3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
